newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- PRICES FADE INTO CLOSE.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- PRICES FADE INTO CLOSE.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds gained ground early but faded to end flat to down 1/8 after a sharp afternoon drop in U.S. Treasuries.
"At the end of the day we just had this sell off," a municipal trader said. "There hasn't been any trading so it's pretty quiet."

Munis had improved by two to three basis points before Treauries' slide. While bonds rose briefly after a good 30-year auction, profit-taking and lack of follow through buying brought the market down. The Treasury's 30-year benchmark bond was down 5/8 at 101-8/32 to yield 6.53 percent in late New York trade.
In debt futures, the September municipal contract closed down 11/32 at 120-6/32. The September T-bond contract closed down 17/32 at 114-7/32. The MOB spread was 191 ticks.
Back in muni cash, price action varied depending on the issue, one trader said.

He cited Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority 5s of 2024, which traded at a 5.45 percent yield on Wednesday. The bonds traded as high as a 5.41 on Thursday morning, but were bid at 5.46 and offered at a 5.44 by Thursday afternoon, he said.

Meanwhile, E-470 Public Highway Authority, Colo., 5s of 2026 which closed at a 5.41 bid, 5.39 offered on Wednesday, saw less movement. The bonds were bid at 5.42 and offered at 5.39 percent on Thursday.
A municipal analyst judged the overall market flat to down 1/8 point at the close. High-grade issues were unchanged except for some short maturities which closed slightly firmer.
Dollar bonds opened a few ticks firmer, and were up 1/8 point by noon. They lost 1/4 point during the afternoon to finish down 1/8, the analyst said.
In new issues, underwriters were able to lower yields on the $453 million Allegheny County, Pa., deal and the $110 million Nassau County, N.Y. deal.

Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover said it repriced Allegheny County's revenue bond deal for Pittsburgh International Airport, lowering yields in several maturities. The offering featured a top yield of 5.52 percent in 2016.
Smith Barney Inc said it repriced $110 million general improvement bonds, cutting yields in several maturities. The deal featured a top yield of 5.04 percent in 2013.
